{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZjEVEg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDJ0Is", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 83, "title": "Implement single-sector µPD765 non-DMA WRITE DATA with byte handshaking", "body": "## Problem

VM and Ap support byte-handshaked non-DMA READ DATA, but WRITE DATA still returns invalid-command status when SPECIFY selects ND=1. Raw floppy clients cannot write through the programmed-I/O interface.

At baseline `e19295865bac9e0d9c07032c10ba2f58242cdd72`, [Bus::finish_fdc](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e19295865bac9e0d9c07032c10ba2f58242cdd72/src/bus.rs#L924) accepts only opcode `46h` in non-DMA mode. [tests/fdc.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e19295865bac9e0d9c07032c10ba2f58242cdd72/tests/fdc.rs#L241) explicitly expects rejection of `45h`. The existing execution state, scheduler and FIFO input path support reads only.

## Expected outcome

Implement one bounded subset: SPECIFY ND=1 followed by single-sector MFM WRITE DATA (`45h`, MT=0), with matching selected head/H, N=1–3 and R=EOT≥1. Support both VM and Ap, both existing floppy drives and either head independently, using existing normal raw/D88 media.

Hardware contract:

- Accept the nine-byte command, then transfer processor-supplied bytes to the matching sector in order. For nonzero N, transfer `128 << N` bytes; DTL does not shorten the transfer. The NEC functional description specifies bytewise writes and applies READ DATA's EN behavior to WRITE DATA. [NEC µPD765A/7265 functional description](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/upd765A.pdf)
- During write execution, CB/EXM are set and DIO is clear: MSR high nibble `30h` while waiting and `B0h` when accepting a byte. Results clear EXM and expose `D0h`, followed by idle `80h` after all seven result bytes. Write protection sets ST1.NW=`02h`; missing sectors set ST1.ND=`04h`; missed service sets ST1.OR=`10h` with abnormal ST0. [NEC µPD765A/B status and instruction tables](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/UPD765_Datasheet_OCRed.pdf#page=9)
- Each requested execution byte generates an interrupt; the servicing data write acknowledges that request. Completion generates a distinct result request. Retain the existing PC-98 slave IR3/master IR7 route and normal PIC EOI requirements. [NEC processor interface and interrupt description](https://www.scribd.com/document/1067140199/UPD765)

Reuse the documented deterministic read scheduling policy: 160 guest clocks for dispatch, first request 128 clocks later, subsequent requests 128 clocks apart, and expiration after 104 unserviced clocks. These are emulator scheduling choices derived from NEC's normal 16 µs and worst-case 13 µs MFM intervals at the repository's 8 MHz guest clock; they do not establish mechanical or instruction-cycle accuracy. Port accesses must not create elapsed time. [NEC Application Note 8, PDF page 2](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/uPD765_App_Note_Mar79.pdf#page=2)

With R=EOT and no TC, terminate after the sector using `ST0=40h|head<<2|drive`, `ST1=80h`, `ST2=0`, followed by the final C/H/R/N. This is the existing repository's explicit EOT-without-TC derivation from EN and sector-ID definitions; the processor-termination table's advanced CHRN row does not apply. [Existing documented derivation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e19295865bac9e0d9c07032c10ba2f58242cdd72/docs/hardware.md#fdc-non-dma-read-data)

For interrupted writes, define a bounded logical-image policy: retain the accepted prefix, leave the unaccepted suffix unchanged, and never change neighboring sectors or D88 metadata. Document this as an image-model approximation; damaged data fields and CRC/flux consequences are not represented. Do not import TC-specific zero filling into a command that received no TC.

## Context and reproduction

Source-derived reproduction, not executed by this evaluator: mount original patterned 77×2×8×1024 media, select `0094h=18h`, issue SPECIFY `03 DF 03`, then `45 00 00 00 02 03 02 1B FF`. After dispatch, current code exposes a one-byte invalid-command result `80h`; the implemented subset should instead enter write execution and request 1,024 bytes.

PR #82 repaired the separate idle BIOS DMA handoff after ND=1. The Coordinator reports all 16 reproduction combinations recovered, 327 native tests passed, and 114 production release-Wasm browser cases passed. Independent PR review and remote CI results were not supplied. These are reported results, not evaluator executions. [Committed validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e19295865bac9e0d9c07032c10ba2f58242cdd72/docs/validation.md#issue-81-bios-floppy-dma-handoff)

The supplied open-Issue list is empty. This behavior is separate from completed Issues #79 and #81. All 26 inventory categories retain their full scopes and supplied statuses: 23 partial, GRCG implemented_unverified, paging/FPU unimplemented, none verified. Protected mode, paging and basic x87 remain required.

Scope excludes multi-sector PIO writes, MT/head switching, deleted-data/format/scan/diagnostic commands, N=0/DTL, new formats, full SPECIFY timing, TC/EOP injection, active BIOS preemption and broader board/mechanical/error fidelity. These remain FDC work, alongside additional media and 512-byte IPL acceptance. The A/B final-byte OR distinction also remains unverified; missed-service acceptance here covers first and interior requests. [NEC A/B differences](https://hxc2001.com/download/datasheet/floppy/thirdparty/FDC/NEC/UPD765_Datasheet_OCRed.pdf#page=5)

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add a focused raw-port regression that fails on the baseline's `45h` rejection and passes with the implementation. Drive commands through ports and guest clocks; do not inject execution state or PIC requests.
- [ ] Verify complete writes on VM/Ap, drives 0/1 and heads 0/1: N=1–3 on original normal-MFM D88 fixtures and N=2/3 across all three existing raw geometries. Independently construct expected media; compare the entire image, including unchanged D88 metadata, neighboring sectors and the other drive. Count one FDC/media write per sector receiving payload, rather than per byte.
- [ ] Assert command/execution/result MSR transitions, exactly one accepted byte per request, and complete seven-byte results. Early or duplicate writes and wrong-direction reads must not consume requests, acknowledge their IRQs or start another command. Drain results before accepting another command. Explicitly reject still-unsupported write variants without media or DMA activity.
- [ ] Test partition-invariant timing, including one-clock ticks and a batch crossing dispatch, availability and timeout. Service at 103 clocks must succeed without moving the next request boundary; service at the 104-clock deadline must fail. Cover first/interior missed requests, exact accepted-prefix media differences, result delivery and fresh-command recovery.
- [ ] Verify byte and distinct result IRQs through the real PIC path, retained ISR until EOI, and no held-request retrigger. Test protected D88 media, absent media and missing sectors without unintended writes. Reset during an accepted prefix or ready request must discard pending execution while retaining already-written bytes; eject during execution must terminate safely.
- [ ] Prove DMA isolation with enabled/unmasked and masked/disabled configurations: preserve current/base addresses and counts, bank, mode, masks, controller enable, shared byte pointer and sticky TC. Guard RAM with data different from the FIFO payload. Preserve ND=0 DMA reads/writes and add completed PIO-write → BIOS readback → fresh ND=1 PIO reentry coverage, retaining PR #82's existing acceptance.
- [ ] Add an original MIT or otherwise licensed source-built interrupt-driven boot probe. Pin source/license, assembly command, firmware/image hashes and independent result/media expectations in a manifest. The guest must issue every command, supply payload, validate readback/results/guards and produce PASS. Run the identical image on native and production release-Wasm VM/Ap, before/after reset, at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, within 2,000,000 slots per boot. Hosts only mount, step, inspect and reset; require exact media changes, IRQ records and no guest/core/browser errors.
- [ ] The Coordinator prepares the documented legal fixtures and runs `cargo test --locked --test fdc --test fdc_bios --test core --test dma --test pic`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and the README's actual production-Wasm/browser checks through `npm test`. Preserve existing DOS/apps/VM/audio, IDE-edge and six-game assertions and budgets. Record exact outcomes, including failures or unexecuted cases; server startup alone is not browser acceptance. Wire the new fixture into existing preparation/CI and document this subset and its remaining limits.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
